data.title: RGA: Saudi Road Code Sets Requirements to Protect Groundwater, Minimize Construction Impact
data.content:
Riyadh, November 22, 2026, SPA -- The Roads General Authority (RGA) affirmed that the Saudi Road Code includes technical requirements aimed at protecting groundwater and minimizing the impact of roadworks on it.
    This reflects RGA’s commitment to balancing road network development across Saudi Arabia’s regions with the preservation of natural resources, while improving quality of life and enhancing safety and efficiency.
    The RGA indicated that the code’s key requirements in this regard include avoiding sensitive aquifers and their boundaries as far as possible when planning and carrying out roadworks, thereby reducing the likelihood of direct harm.
    They also include setting limits on the volume, depth, and duration of temporary pumping during construction to ensure that accumulated or extracted water is managed in accordance with assessments that preserve the site’s water balance.
    The RGA added that the code restricts the use of construction methods that could damage aquifers.
    It also includes requirements for monitoring water levels in nearby wells or surface water bodies where necessary to track any changes that may result from the works and address them in a timely manner before they worsen.
    The RGA noted that the code supports its strategy of establishing a unified legislative and regulatory framework for the road sector by standardizing technical and operational requirements and enabling road-owning entities to systematically and sustainably improve the quality of their work.
    This is achieved through comprehensive standards covering all stages of a road’s life cycle, from design and construction to operation and ongoing maintenance, within a unified regulatory framework that ensures the highest levels of efficiency and safety.
    
    -- SPA
